description: Site: oscal/emit.rs:733-753 (uuid_v8). The workspace derives every OSCAL UUID from a (namespace, seed) tuple via SHA-256, masking the version (8) and variant (10b) bits in place. This gives byte-identical OSCAL output for identical inputs across runs, which is what makes CI diffability and evidence-pack reproducibility actually work. Why this is correct and what a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing: a contributor will eventually say 'just use the uuid crate.' Don't. The uuid crate's v4 (random) and v7 (time-based) UUIDs both break determinism by design; v5 (SHA-1-derived) would introduce a SHA-1 dep that the workspace explicitly avoids; v8 with arbitrary data is exactly what we have, written in 20 lines of code with no external dependency. The pkix-lint emitter is bit-for-bit reproducible because of this choice. The version+variant nibble masking is correct per RFC 9562 §5.8 (version 8 = 1000b in bits 48..52; variant 10b in bits 64..66) — verified by the unit tests in this module.
title: Deterministic UUID derivation (RFC 9562 UUIDv8 over SHA-256) — defend against 'just use uuid crate'
